A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEPT framework, authors, three variants, and core experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pile and MC4 experiments, generalization and adaptation results, and a billion-parameter federated-training demonstration, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original DEPT experiments and reports additional downstream evaluations, IID C4 experiments, and comparisons with isolated models and Pythia.

M1.justification: GLOB, TRIM, and SPEC retain the same local-training, aggregation, and embedding-sharing procedures. v4 explicitly includes positional embeddings in Algorithm 1 and explains trimming/projection mathematically, but these operations were already described in v1. SPEC-OPT also existed in v1.

E1.justification: Alongside the retained Pile and MC4 coverage, v4 adds IID C4 training through random sharding (Appendix B.3) and downstream evaluation on MNLI, RACE, STSB, and SST-2 (Tables 7 and 21). This extends evaluation beyond language-model perplexity and multilingual adaptation to several supervised language-understanding tasks.

E2.justification: v4 adds independently trained, unmerged single-source models (Tables 14–17) and Pythia-160M/410M (Tables 18–20). Corresponding retained comparisons also change membership: the 24-block Pile random-initialization comparison includes both uniform and proportional STD baselines, whereas v1 Tables 3–4 report only proportional sampling.

E3.justification: v4 adds supervised fine-tuning protocols with accuracy and Pearson correlation, an IID sharding control, token-matched isolated-model comparisons, and explicit comparisons of continued-pretraining sampling policies. It also reports unigram cross-entropy. The reported baseline design now specifies learning-rate tuning to complete equal training schedules, whereas v1 emphasizes longer DEPT training and selection of nondiverged baseline checkpoints.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether benefits persist on IID data (Figure 7), what aggregation contributes relative to isolated training (Appendix B.8), and how continued-pretraining sampling affects results (Tables 3, 5, 10, and 11). The multilingual adaptation curves and billion-scale client-subsampling demonstration already appeared in v1 and are not new analyses.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly describes the DEPT summary curves as average ± min/max (Figure 3) and introduces mean ± sigma summaries of vocabulary sizes across data sources (Tables 2 and 9). v1 already displayed shaded average curves without this explanation. These are limited descriptive-reporting additions; neither version provides seed counts, repeated-run confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds downstream, IID, isolated-model, Pythia, and sampling-comparison results and revises retained entries. For example, MC4 Swahili random-initialization perplexities change from 36.3 to 35.2 for GLOB and from 35.2 to 46.3 for ACT (v1 Table 1; v4 Table 4). These are revised reported values, not established same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: v4 replaces v1's embedding-memory reduction expression with a parameter-saving expression proportional to the global-minus-local vocabulary size and adds explicit memory and communication complexity formulas in Table 1. This is a limited mathematical correction and extension; no convergence theorem or proof is added, and the trimming equations largely formalize the existing procedure.

C1.justification: The central claims about vocabulary-independent training, robustness, efficiency, generalization, and plasticity remain. v4 adds an explicit downstream language-understanding improvement claim, quantifies average perplexity improvements, and refines communication savings as dependent on synchronization frequency and embedding size rather than emphasizing v1's fixed 675-fold headline.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies v1's broad pretrained-embedding outperformance claims by acknowledging MC4 OOD underperformance and weaker small-model results, discussing sampling and aggregation as possible explanations. It also adds interpretations of isolated-model and Pythia results, acknowledges incomplete hyperparameter optimization, and explains the applicability limits of using local versus global SPEC embeddings (Appendices A, B, and F).

D1.justification: v1's sparse, partly unfinished experimental appendix becomes a detailed account of architecture, batch sizes, sequence length, optimizer settings, schedules, local steps, source sampling, and vocabulary sizes. v4 additionally documents baseline tuning, ACT adaptation, MosaicML/Flower software, GPU hardware, and downstream fine-tuning recipes. Much of this is newly disclosed implementation information rather than evidence of a changed method.

R1.justification: v4 adds targeted connections to adaptive pretraining, training instability and local-SGD regularization, vocabulary trimming, and embedding transfer or stitching, including Gururangan, Wortsman, Lin, Ushio, Xu, Remy, and Moschella. The central positioning relative to multilingual pretraining, federated/local SGD, and active forgetting remains; several of those relationships already appeared in v1's appendices.

P1.justification: The introduction and method discussion are extensively rewritten and condensed. Experimental design and results become separate sections, generalization is divided into transformer-body, pretrained-embedding, and downstream discussions, related work is consolidated, and appendices are reorganized and expanded. These are substantial narrative changes beyond inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: The original pipeline illustration is replaced by a numbered four-panel diagram. Split result tables are consolidated and redesigned with distribution groupings, averages, unigram cross-entropies, and improvement rows. Existing plots are restyled with inset zooms and redistributed between the main text and appendices; new cost, baseline, and downstream tables substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially addresses v1's incomplete experimental documentation and limited evidence for practical generalization through detailed training specifications, downstream tasks, IID controls, and isolated-model comparisons. Its discussion also better acknowledges pretrained-embedding failures and sampling dependence. Reporting problems remain, including Table 20's initialization-caption inconsistency and the erroneous '500× memory' wording in Section 4.2, but the gains in reproducibility, experimental scrutiny, and interpretation are substantial overall.
